history.origins: Played in parts of the Eastern USA (North Carolina, Tennessee). Often home-made with a second deck cut and glued to form the board. Jax published a commercial version in 1982 under the name Sequence.
timeline: Pre-1982: Folk game with home-made boards in Eastern USA.
1982: Jax publishes Sequence as a commercial board game.
2003: Quinto (Quinto Game Company) releases variant with scoring system.
Present: Sequence remains popular; One-Eyed Jack name used for the traditional card-driven version.
history.cultural: Regional Eastern US favourite. The one-eyed vs two-eyed jack distinction (remove vs wild) is the game's defining mechanic.
history.evolution: From folk game with cut-and-glue boards to commercial Sequence. Double Series (Jouets Bo-Jeux) and Quinto offer alternative formats.

setup.players: 2, 3, or 4 players. Four typically play as partners (opposite seats).
setup.deck: Two standard 52-card packs (104 cards). Board: 50 card-spaces from a second deck (4 jacks removed; 2 jokers = corner spaces).
setup.dealing: 1. Deal 7 (2 players), 6 (3 players), or 5 (4 players) cards to each player. 2. Remaining cards form the stock.
setup.equipment: Two decks, board (10x10 with card faces in cells; jokers in corners), chips: 50 per colour (2 players/teams) or 40 per colour (3 players).

rules.objective: Form one or more rows of five chips of your colour (or your team's) on the board. Rows can be horizontal, vertical, or diagonal.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Turn**: Play one card face-up, place a chip on the matching unoccupied board space (or use jack power). 2. **Draw**: Replenish hand from stock. 3. **Two-eyed jack** (clubs, diamonds): Wildâ€”place your chip on any unoccupied space. 4. **One-eyed jack** (hearts, spades): Remove one opponent chip from the board. 5. **Win**: First player/team to complete a row of five chips wins.
keyRules: Play card â†’ place chip on matching space (or use jack).
Two-eyed jack = place chip on any empty space.
One-eyed jack = remove one opponent chip.
Draw at end of turn. Play proceeds clockwise from dealer's left.
Corner joker spaces: rules vary (free space, wild, or special).

strategy.basic: Block opponents' rows. Use two-eyed jacks for hard-to-reach spaces. Save one-eyed jacks to break an opponent's four-in-a-row.
strategy.intermediate: Build multiple threats (two rows of four). Force opponents to block while you advance another line.
strategy.advanced: Partner coordination: one blocks, one builds. Track which cards are dead (both spaces occupied).
tips: Corners and edges can be valuableâ€”fewer directions for opponents to block.
Dead cards (both spaces filled): some variants allow discard-and-draw; agree before play.

variations.description: If both spaces for a card are occupied, holder may discard it and draw a replacement (does not count as a turn).

scoring.description: No scoring in basic game. First to form a row of five wins.
scoring.winCondition: First player or team to complete a row of five chips (horizontal, vertical, or diagonal) wins.

synthesis.shortDescription: Place chips on a 10x10 card board by playing matching cards. Two-eyed jacks = wild; one-eyed jacks remove opponent chips. First to five in a row wins.
